claim: The study mapped the developmental origin of 160 interneurons from seven bilateral neural progenitors (neuroblasts) in the Drosophila larval central nervous system.
source: To address this, we mapped the developmental origin of 160 interneurons from seven bilateral neural progenitors (neuroblasts) and identify them in a synapse-scale TEM reconstruction of the Drosophila larval central nervous system.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the number of neurons mapped and their origin.

claim: Lineages concurrently build sensory and motor neuropils by generating sensory and motor hemilineages in a Notch-dependent manner.
source: We find that lineages concurrently build the sensory and motor neuropils by generating sensory and motor hemilineages in a Notch-dependent manner.
evidence: The abstract directly states this finding about hemilineage generation.

claim: Neurons in a hemilineage share common synaptic targeting within the neuropil.
source: Neurons in a hemilineage share common synaptic targeting within the neuropil, which is further refined based on neuronal temporal identity.
evidence: The abstract explicitly describes this property of hemilineages.

claim: Hemilineage-temporal cohorts share common connectivity.
source: Connectome analysis shows that hemilineage-temporal cohorts share common connectivity.
evidence: The abstract states this finding from connectome analysis.

claim: Proximity alone cannot explain the observed connectivity structure.
source: Finally, we show that proximity alone cannot explain the observed connectivity structure, suggesting hemilineage/temporal identity confers an added layer of specificity.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this conclusion about connectivity.

claim: Spatial patterning genes act combinatorially to establish unique neuroblast identities in Drosophila.
source: The first step occurs when spatial patterning genes act combinatorially to establish single, unique progenitor (neuroblast) identities (Skeath and Thor, 2003).
evidence: The introduction cites prior work establishing this mechanism.

claim: Drosophila embryonic neuroblasts undergo a cascade of temporal transcription factors: Hunchback (Hb), Krüppel (Kr), Pdm, and Castor (Cas).
source: Here, we focus on Drosophila embryonic neuroblasts, which undergo a cascade of temporal transcription factors: Hunchback (Hb), Krüppel (Kr), Pdm, and Castor (Cas) (Isshiki et al., 2001).
evidence: The introduction cites prior work describing the temporal transcription factor cascade.

claim: Each temporal transcription factor is inherited by ganglion mother cells (GMCs) born during each expression window.
source: Each temporal transcription factor is inherited by ganglion mother cells (GMCs) born during each expression window.
evidence: The introduction describes the inheritance mechanism.

claim: Hemilineages are formed by GMC asymmetric division into a pair of post-mitotic neurons.
source: Hemilineages are formed by GMC asymmetric division into a pair of post-mitotic neurons; during this division, the Notch inhibitor Numb (Nb) is partitioned into one neuron (NotchOFF neuron), whereas the other sibling neuron receives active Notch signaling (NotchON neuron), thereby establishing NotchON and NotchOFF hemilineages (Figure 1A, right).
evidence: The introduction describes the mechanism of hemilineage formation.

claim: The Notch inhibitor Numb is partitioned into one neuron during GMC division, creating a NotchOFF neuron.
source: Hemilineages are formed by GMC asymmetric division into a pair of post-mitotic neurons; during this division, the Notch inhibitor Numb (Nb) is partitioned into one neuron (NotchOFF neuron), whereas the other sibling neuron receives active Notch signaling (NotchON neuron), thereby establishing NotchON and NotchOFF hemilineages (Figure 1A, right).
evidence: The introduction describes Numb partitioning during division.

claim: Three mechanisms generate neuronal diversity within the embryonic CNS: neuroblast spatial identity, GMC temporal identity, and neuronal hemilineage identity.
source: In summary, three mechanisms generate neuronal diversity within the embryonic central nervous system (CNS): neuroblast spatial identity, GMC temporal identity, and neuronal hemilineage identity.
evidence: The introduction summarizes the three mechanisms.

claim: Neurons initially target their axons to broad regions followed by targeting to a neuropil domain and finally forming highly specific synapses.
source: Neurons initially target their axons to broad regions (e.g., thalamus/cortex), followed by targeting to a neuropil domain (glomeruli/layer), and finally forming highly specific synapses within the targeted domain (Kolodkin and Tessier-Lavigne, 2011; Moyle et al., 2021).
evidence: The introduction cites prior work on neural circuit formation mechanisms.

claim: The study analyzed over a quarter of the ~300 neurons per hemisegment.
source: We map the developmental origin for 80 bilateral pairs of interneurons in abdominal segment 1 (A1) by identifying and reconstructing these neurons within a full CNS TEM volume (Ohyama et al., 2015); this is over a quarter of the ~300 neurons per hemisegment.
evidence: The introduction states the proportion of neurons analyzed.

claim: Individual neuroblast lineages have unique but broad axon and dendrite projections to both motor and sensory neuropil.
source: Our results show that individual neuroblast lineages have unique but broad axon and dendrite projections to both motor and sensory neuropil; hemilineages restrict projections and synapse localization to either motor or sensory neuropil; and distinct temporal identities within hemilineages provide additional specificity in synapse localization and connectivity.
evidence: The introduction summarizes the main findings about lineage projections.

claim: All assayed neuroblast clones had a reproducible clonal morphology including the number of fascicles entering the neuropil, cell body position, and axon/dendrite morphology.
source: All assayed neuroblast clones had a reproducible clonal morphology including the number of fascicles entering the neuropil, cell body position, and axon/dendrite morphology (Figure 1B; data not shown).
evidence: The results section describes the reproducibility of clonal morphology.

claim: The similarity in overall clone morphology between genetically marked clones and TEM reconstructed clones was obvious.
source: The similarity in overall clone morphology between genetically marked clones and TEM reconstructed clones was obvious (compare Figure 1B, C).
evidence: The results section states the similarity and references figures showing this.

claim: The same seven lineages were reconstructed in a second hemisegment (A1R) with similar neuron numbers, similar fascicles per clone, and similar clonal morphology.
source: Second, we reconstructed the same seven lineages in a second hemisegment, A1R. We observed similar neuron numbers, similar fascicles per clone, and similar clonal morphology (Figure 1E; data not shown).
evidence: The results section describes validation in a second hemisegment.

claim: Neuroblast lineages are highly stereotyped in left and right hemisegments.
source: Thus, neuroblast lineages are highly stereotyped in left and right hemisegments.
evidence: The results section concludes about lineage stereotypy.

claim: Clonally related neurons project widely and localize synapses widely.
source: We conclude that clonally related neurons project widely and localize synapses widely (Figure 1G, H).
evidence: The results section concludes about clonal neuron projections.

claim: The study mapped 14 neuroblast clones in the TEM volume (seven in A1L, seven in A1R).
source: In total, we have mapped 14 neuroblast clones in the TEM volume (seven in A1L, seven in A1R).
evidence: The results section states the total number of clones mapped.

claim: The mapped lineages contain 160 interneurons (80 each in A1l and A1r), containing 7794 presynapses and 19,468 postsynapses.
source: These lineages contain 160 interneurons (80 each in A1l and A1r), containing 7794 presynapses and 19,468 postsynapses.
evidence: The results section provides quantitative data on neurons and synapses.

claim: In Drosophila, motor dendrites target a dorsal region of the neuropil, while sensory neurons target a ventral region of the neuropil.
source: In Drosophila, motor dendrites target a dorsal region of the neuropil, while sensory neurons target a ventral region of the neuropil (Landgraf et al., 2003; Mauss et al., 2009; Zarin et al., 2019; Zlatic et al., 2009).
evidence: The results section cites prior work on neuropil organization.

claim: Premotor neurons target pre- and postsynapses to the dorsal neuropil.
source: We extend these findings to show that premotor neurons also target pre- and postsynapses to the dorsal neuropil, and targets of sensory afferents target pre- and postsynapses to the ventral neuropil (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: The results section describes new findings about premotor neuron targeting.

claim: Targets of sensory afferents target pre- and postsynapses to the ventral neuropil.
source: We extend these findings to show that premotor neurons also target pre- and postsynapses to the dorsal neuropil, and targets of sensory afferents target pre- and postsynapses to the ventral neuropil (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: The results section describes new findings about sensory target neuron targeting.

claim: The neuropil has an important functional subdivision along the dorsoventral axis.
source: Thus, the neuropil has an important functional subdivision along the dorsoventral axis.
evidence: The results section concludes about neuropil organization.

claim: Nearly all neuroblasts made two morphologically distinct types of neurons (except NB2-1).
source: Upon examination of each lineage, we found that nearly all neuroblasts made two morphologically distinct types of neurons (except NB2-1; Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The results section describes the morphological diversity within lineages.

claim: Most lineages made two distinct morphological classes of neurons using NBLAST analysis.
source: We used NBLAST (Costa et al., 2016) to quantify the morphological similarity of neurons within each neuroblast lineage and found that most lineages made two distinct morphological classes of neurons (or one class of neurons plus glia).
evidence: The results section describes NBLAST analysis results.

claim: Each neuronal class projected to the dorsal/motor neuropil or the ventral/sensory neuropil.
source: Strikingly, each neuronal class projected to the dorsal/motor neuropil or the ventral/sensory neuropil (Figure 2D–H).
evidence: The results section describes the projection patterns of morphological classes.

claim: NB3-3 had only one fascicle at the NBLAST threshold used, and all neurons were ventral-projecting.
source: Note that NB3-3 had only one fascicle at the NBLAST threshold used, and all neurons were ventral-projecting (Figure 2I).
evidence: The results section describes the exception of NB3-3.

claim: Most lineages generate two distinct classes of neurons that target either the ventral/sensory or dorsal/motor neuropils.
source: We conclude that most lineages generate two distinct classes of neurons that target either the ventral/sensory or dorsal/motor neuropils (Figure 2J).
evidence: The results section concludes about lineage organization.

claim: Within the larval and adult CNS most neuroblast lineages generate NotchON neurons with a similar clonal morphology and NotchOFF hemilineage with a different morphology.
source: Recent work has shown that within the larval and adult CNS most neuroblast lineages generate NotchON neurons with a similar clonal morphology (called the NotchON hemilineage), and NotchOFF hemilineage with a different morphology (Harris et al., 2015; Lacin and Truman, 2016; Lee et al., 2020; Truman et al., 2010).
evidence: The results section cites prior work on hemilineages.

claim: NB3-3 makes only one 'NotchOFF' hemilineage via type 0 divisions.
source: This hypothesis was strengthened by the fact that the sole neuroblast lineage that generated a single morphological class, NB3-3, had previously been shown to make only one 'NotchOFF' hemilineage via type 0 divisions (Baumgardt et al., 2014; Wreden et al., 2017).
evidence: The results section cites prior work on NB3-3.

claim: Each neuroblast makes a NotchON hemilineage projecting to the dorsal motor neuropil (or glia), and a NotchOFF hemilineage projecting to the ventral sensory neuropil.
source: Based on these data, we hypothesize that each neuroblast makes a NotchON hemilineage projecting to the dorsal motor neuropil (or glia), and a NotchOFF hemilineage projecting to the ventral sensory neuropil.
evidence: The results section states the hypothesis about hemilineage projections.

claim: NotchON neurons specifically project to the dorsal motor neuropil in NB5-2 and NB7-1 lineages.
source: This resulted in specific labeling of dorsal projecting neurons within the NB5-2 lineage (Figure 3A, A') or the NB7-1 lineage (Figure 3B, B').
evidence: The results section describes experimental results with Notch reporter.

claim: Notch activity determines dorsal/ventral neuropil projections.
source: We next asked whether Notch activity determines dorsal/ventral neuropil projections.
evidence: The results section states the question being tested.

claim: Notch expression throughout the NB1-2, NB5-2, or NB7-1 lineages led to a re-routing of projections from the ventral neuropil to the dorsal neuropil.
source: In contrast, Notch expression throughout the NB1-2, NB5-2, or NB7-1 lineages led to a re-routing of projections from the ventral neuropil to the dorsal neuropil (Figure 3G–I).
evidence: The results section describes experimental results of Notch misexpression.

claim: Notch expression throughout the NB7-4 lineage led to a loss of ventral projecting neurons and an increase in glia.
source: Notch expression throughout the NB7-4 lineage led to a loss of ventral projecting neurons and an increase in glia (Figure 3J).
evidence: The results section describes experimental results for NB7-4.

claim: Ascending and descending projection neurons are normally generated by ventral NotchOFF hemilineages.
source: In addition, we note that ascending and descending projection neurons are normally generated by ventral NotchOFF hemilineages (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The results section describes the origin of projection neurons.

claim: Ascending and descending projection neurons were completely lost following Notchintra expression.
source: Importantly, these ascending and descending projection neurons were completely lost following Notchintra expression (Figure 3G–I, insets).
evidence: The results section describes the effect of Notch misexpression on projection neurons.

claim: NotchOFF hemilineages make more complex and lengthy neurons than the NotchON hemilineages.
source: Our observation that NotchOFF hemilineages make more complex and lengthy neurons than the NotchON hemilineages is similar to that observed for larval brain lineages (Lee et al., 2020), suggesting that this is a conserved mechanism.
evidence: The results section compares findings to prior work.

claim: The same number of neurons were observed in control versus Notchintra embryos at stage 16/17 for NB1-2, NB5-2, NB7-1, and NB7-4.
source: The Notchintra phenotypes we observed are likely due to a NotchOFF to NotchON hemilineage transformation, rather than death of ventral projecting neurons, as we observed the same number of neurons in control versus Notchintra embryos at stage 16/17 (NB1-2 control: 12.2, n = 10 hemisegments; NB1-2 Notchintra: 14.1, n = 12 [p=0.0785]; NB5-2 control: 20.3, n = 16 hemisegments; NB5-2 Notchintra: 19.3, n = 26 [p=0.2311]; NB7-1 control: 18.9, n = 7 hemisegments; NB7-1 Notchintra: 19.8, n = 11 [p=0.6166]; NB7-4 control: 8.6, n = 9 hemisegments; NB7-4 Notchintra: 9.5, n = 11 [p=0.1710]).
evidence: The results section provides quantitative data on neuron numbers.

claim: NBLAST can be used to accurately identify neuroblast hemilineages.
source: In conclusion, we show that NBLAST can be used to accurately identify neuroblast hemilineages; that NotchON/NotchOFF hemilineages project to motor/sensory neuropil domains, respectively; and most importantly, that hemilineage identity determines neuronal targeting to the motor or sensory neuropil.
evidence: The results section concludes about NBLAST utility.

claim: Hemilineage identity determines neuronal targeting to the motor or sensory neuropil.
source: In conclusion, we show that NBLAST can be used to accurately identify neuroblast hemilineages; that NotchON/NotchOFF hemilineages project to motor/sensory neuropil domains, respectively; and most importantly, that hemilineage identity determines neuronal targeting to the motor or sensory neuropil.
evidence: The results section concludes about hemilineage function.

claim: Each neuroblast coordinately generates similar numbers of sensory and motor processing neurons throughout its embryonic lineage.
source: Thus, each neuroblast coordinately generates similar numbers of sensory and motor processing neurons throughout its embryonic lineage.
evidence: The results section concludes about neuroblast function.

claim: Neurons in dorsal hemilineages localized both presynapses and postsynapses to dorsal neuropil.
source: We found that the neurons in dorsal hemilineages localized both pre- and postsynaptic sites to the dorsal/motor neuropil, whereas neurons in ventral hemilineages localized both pre- and postsynaptic sites to the ventral/sensory neuropil (Figure 4A).
evidence: The results section describes synapse localization patterns.

claim: Neurons in ventral hemilineages localized both presynapses and postsynapses to ventral neuropil.
source: We found that the neurons in dorsal hemilineages localized both pre- and postsynaptic sites to the dorsal/motor neuropil, whereas neurons in ventral hemilineages localized both pre- and postsynaptic sites to the ventral/sensory neuropil (Figure 4A).
evidence: The results section describes synapse localization patterns.

claim: The vast majority of sensory output was to ventral hemilineages.
source: Consistent with these observations, we found that the vast majority of sensory output was to ventral hemilineages, and the vast majority of input to motor neurons was from dorsal hemilineages (Figure 4B).
evidence: The results section describes connectivity patterns.

claim: The vast majority of input to motor neurons was from dorsal hemilineages.
source: Consistent with these observations, we found that the vast majority of sensory output was to ventral hemilineages, and the vast majority of input to motor neurons was from dorsal hemilineages (Figure 4B).
evidence: The results section describes connectivity patterns.

claim: NotchON hemilineages target projections and pre- and postsynapses to the motor neuropil.
source: We conclude that, at least for the assayed hemilineages, NotchON hemilineages target projections and pre- and postsynapses to the motor neuropil, whereas NotchOFF hemilineages target projections and pre- and postsynapses to the sensory neuropil (Figure 4H).
evidence: The results section concludes about hemilineage targeting.

claim: NotchOFF hemilineages target projections and pre- and postsynapses to the sensory neuropil.
source: We conclude that, at least for the assayed hemilineages, NotchON hemilineages target projections and pre- and postsynapses to the motor neuropil, whereas NotchOFF hemilineages target projections and pre- and postsynapses to the sensory neuropil (Figure 4H).
evidence: The results section concludes about hemilineage targeting.

claim: Presynapses were localized to distinct regions of the neuropil for individual hemilineages.
source: We found that presynapses were localized to distinct regions of the neuropil (Figure 4C, D).
evidence: The results section describes presynapse localization.

claim: Postsynapses were localized to distinct but slightly more overlapping regions of the neuropil.
source: Similarly, postsynapses were localized to distinct but slightly more overlapping regions of the neuropil (Figure 4E, F).
evidence: The results section describes postsynapse localization.

claim: Synapses from lineages in A1L and A1R had similar relative positions in the neuropil.
source: We found that synapses from lineages in A1L and A1R had similar relative positions in the neuropil (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–D), highlighting the stereotypy of synapse localization.
evidence: The results section describes left-right stereotypy.

claim: Neurons in a hemilineage showed greater similarity in synaptic positions (pre or post) than unrelated neurons.
source: Importantly, neurons in a hemilineage showed greater similarity in synaptic positions (pre or post) than unrelated neurons (Figure 4G, Figure 4—figure supplement 1E, F).
evidence: The results section describes synapse similarity within hemilineages.

claim: Each hemilineage targets its presynapses (and to a lesser extent postsynapses) to small domains of the sensory or motor neuropil.
source: We conclude that each hemilineage targets its presynapses (and to a lesser extent postsynapses) to small domains of the sensory or motor neuropil (Figure 4H), strongly suggesting that the developmental information needed for neuropil targeting is shared by neurons in a hemilineage, but not by all neurons in a complete neuroblast lineage (see Discussion).
evidence: The results section concludes about hemilineage targeting specificity.

claim: Temporal transcription factors (Hb, Kr, Pdm, and Cas) have a radial distribution in the embryonic CNS.
source: First, we confirmed that temporal transcription factors (Hb, Kr, Pdm, and Cas) have a radial distribution in the embryonic CNS, with early-born Hb+ neurons positioned in a deep layer adjacent to the developing neuropil and late-born Cas+ neurons are at the most superficial position within the CNS (Isshiki et al., 2001; Kambadur et al., 1998; Figure 5A).
evidence: The results section confirms prior findings about temporal factor distribution.

claim: Early-born Hb+ neurons are positioned in a deep layer adjacent to the developing neuropil.
source: First, we confirmed that temporal transcription factors (Hb, Kr, Pdm, and Cas) have a radial distribution in the embryonic CNS, with early-born Hb+ neurons positioned in a deep layer adjacent to the developing neuropil and late-born Cas+ neurons are at the most superficial position within the CNS (Isshiki et al., 2001; Kambadur et al., 1998; Figure 5A).
evidence: The results section describes Hb+ neuron position.

claim: Late-born Cas+ neurons are at the most superficial position within the CNS.
source: First, we confirmed that temporal transcription factors (Hb, Kr, Pdm, and Cas) have a radial distribution in the embryonic CNS, with early-born Hb+ neurons positioned in a deep layer adjacent to the developing neuropil and late-born Cas+ neurons are at the most superficial position within the CNS (Isshiki et al., 2001; Kambadur et al., 1998; Figure 5A).
evidence: The results section describes Cas+ neuron position.

claim: The radial distribution of temporal factors persists for more stable Hb and Cas reporters in the newly hatched larval CNS.
source: Importantly, we show that this distribution persists for more stable Hb and Cas reporters in the newly hatched larval CNS (Figure 5B, C), the stage of the TEM reconstruction.
evidence: The results section describes persistence of radial distribution.

claim: Radial position can be used as a proxy for temporal identity in both embryos and newly hatched larvae.
source: Thus, radial position can be used as a proxy for temporal identity in both embryos and newly hatched larvae (Figure 5D).
evidence: The results section concludes about using radial position as a proxy.

claim: The study identified 54 Hb+ neurons and 44 Cas+ neurons within the TEM volume.
source: In total, we identified 54 Hb+ neurons and 44 Cas+ neurons within the TEM volume.
evidence: The results section provides quantitative data on identified neurons.

claim: Experimentally verified Hb+ neurons were closer to the neuropil, whereas Cas+ neurons were further from the neuropil.
source: We measured their cortex neurite length (neurite length from the cell body to the neuropil entry point; i.e., the length of the neurite as it traverses the cellular cortex) and found that experimentally verified Hb+ neurons were closer to the neuropil, whereas Cas+ neurons were further from the neuropil (Figure 5G).
evidence: The results section describes the relationship between temporal identity and cortex neurite length.

claim: Neuronal radial position can be used as a proxy for neuronal temporal identity.
source: We conclude that neuronal radial position can be used as a proxy for neuronal temporal identity.
evidence: The results section concludes about using radial position.

claim: The same neuron in A1L and A1R had similar cortex neurite lengths.
source: Importantly, the same neuron in A1L and A1R had similar cortex neurite lengths (Figure 5H), showing that cell body radial position was reproducible.
evidence: The results section describes left-right reproducibility.

claim: 70 interneurons were assigned to one of four temporal cohorts (early, mid-early, mid-late, and late born) based on radial position.
source: We assigned 70 interneurons to one of four temporal cohorts (early, mid-early, mid-late, and late born) based on radial position (Figure 5I).
evidence: The results section describes temporal cohort assignment.

claim: Cortex neurite length can be used as a proxy for temporal identity and is reproducible across at least two hemisegments.
source: We conclude that cortex neurite length can be used as a proxy for temporal identity, that it is reproducible across at least two hemisegments, and that it can be used to approximate the temporal identity of any neuron in the TEM reconstruction.
evidence: The results section concludes about cortex neurite length as a proxy.

claim: Neurons with a shared temporal identity had broad neuronal projections.
source: We found that neurons in each temporal class had broad neuronal projections, and no greater than unrelated neurons synapse similarity (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The results section describes temporal cohort projections.

claim: Temporal identity, on its own, does not confer shared neuronal projections or synapse localization.
source: We conclude that temporal identity, on its own, does not confer shared neuronal projections or synapse localization.
evidence: The results section concludes about temporal identity alone.

claim: NB5-2 dorsal hemilineage-temporal cohorts target their presynapses to mostly non-overlapping neuropil domains.
source: We found that NB5-2 dorsal hemilineage-temporal cohorts target their presynapses to mostly non-overlapping neuropil domains (Figure 6A), whereas the NB3-3 hemilineage-temporal cohorts target their postsynapses to mostly non-overlapping neuropil domains (Figure 6B).
evidence: The results section describes hemilineage-temporal cohort targeting.

claim: NB3-3 hemilineage-temporal cohorts target their postsynapses to mostly non-overlapping neuropil domains.
source: We found that NB5-2 dorsal hemilineage-temporal cohorts target their presynapses to mostly non-overlapping neuropil domains (Figure 6A), whereas the NB3-3 hemilineage-temporal cohorts target their postsynapses to mostly non-overlapping neuropil domains (Figure 6B).
evidence: The results section describes hemilineage-temporal cohort targeting.

claim: Hemilineage-temporal cohorts had more similar synaptic positions than hemilineage alone.
source: When we expand this analysis to all hemilineages, we found that (a) hemilineage-temporal cohorts had more similar synaptic positions than hemilineage alone, and (b) dorsal hemilineage-temporal cohorts preferentially clustered presynapses, whereas ventral hemilineage-temporal cohorts preferentially clustered postsynapses (Figure 6C–F).
evidence: The results section describes synapse clustering in hemilineage-temporal cohorts.

claim: Dorsal hemilineage-temporal cohorts preferentially clustered presynapses.
source: When we expand this analysis to all hemilineages, we found that (a) hemilineage-temporal cohorts had more similar synaptic positions than hemilineage alone, and (b) dorsal hemilineage-temporal cohorts preferentially clustered presynapses, whereas ventral hemilineage-temporal cohorts preferentially clustered postsynapses (Figure 6C–F).
evidence: The results section describes presynapse clustering in dorsal hemilineages.

claim: Ventral hemilineage-temporal cohorts preferentially clustered postsynapses.
source: When we expand this analysis to all hemilineages, we found that (a) hemilineage-temporal cohorts had more similar synaptic positions than hemilineage alone, and (b) dorsal hemilineage-temporal cohorts preferentially clustered presynapses, whereas ventral hemilineage-temporal cohorts preferentially clustered postsynapses (Figure 6C–F).
evidence: The results section describes postsynapse clustering in ventral hemilineages.

claim: Temporal identity subdivides hemilineages into smaller populations of neurons that target both projections and synapses to distinct subdomains within the larger hemilineage targeting domain.
source: We conclude that temporal identity subdivides hemilineages into smaller populations of neurons that target both projections and synapses to distinct subdomains within the larger hemilineage targeting domain (Figure 6G).
evidence: The results section concludes about temporal identity function.

claim: Hemilineage identity provides coarse targeting within the neuropil, and temporal identity refines targeting to smaller subdomains.
source: Thus, hemilineage identity provides coarse targeting within the neuropil, and temporal identity refines targeting to smaller subdomains.
evidence: The results section concludes about the hierarchical targeting mechanism.

claim: The three Eve+ neurons at the core of the proprioceptive circuit are from a single hemilineage-temporal cohort: late-born neurons from the NB3-3 hemilineage.
source: Recent work has shown that the three Eve+ interneurons at the core of the circuit are from a single hemilineage-temporal cohort: late-born neurons from the NB3-3 hemilineage (Wreden et al., 2017).
evidence: The results section cites prior work on the Eve circuit.

claim: The Jaam neurons are all derived from a single hemilineage-temporal cohort: late-born neuron in the NB5-2 ventral (NotchOFF) hemilineage.
source: In addition, we find that the Jaam neurons are all derived from a single hemilineage-temporal cohort: late-born neuron in the NB5-2 ventral (NotchOFF) hemilineage (Figure 9B; Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The results section describes the developmental origin of Jaam neurons.

claim: All three Saaghi neurons are derived from a single hemilineage-temporal cohort: late-born neuron in the NB5-2 dorsal (NotchON) hemilineage.
source: Similarly, all three Saaghi neurons are derived from a single hemilineage-temporal cohort: late-born neuron in the NB5-2 dorsal (NotchON) hemilineage (Figure 9B; Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The results section describes the developmental origin of Saaghi neurons.

claim: The Jaam-EL-Saaghi proprioceptive circuit is assembled from three distinct hemilineage-temporal cohorts.
source: Thus, the Jaam-EL-Saaghi proprioceptive circuit is assembled from three distinct hemilineage-temporal cohorts (Figure 9C).
evidence: The results section concludes about the circuit composition.

claim: Other motor circuits may also be assembled by preferential connectivity between distinct hemilineage-temporal cohorts.
source: We propose that other motor circuits may also be assembled by preferential connectivity between distinct hemilineage-temporal cohorts.
evidence: The results section proposes a general principle.

claim: In mammals, clonally related neurons often have a similar location.
source: In mammals, clonally related neurons often have a similar location (Fekete et al., 1994; Mihalas and Hevner, 2018), morphology (Mihalas and Hevner, 2018; Wong and Rapaport, 2009), and connectivity (Yu et al., 2009).
evidence: The discussion cites prior work on mammalian clonal neurons.

claim: Clonally related neurons in Drosophila project widely in the neuropil, to both sensory and motor domains, and thus lack shared morphology.
source: In contrast, we found that clonally related neurons project widely in the neuropil, to both sensory and motor domains, and thus lack shared morphology.
evidence: The discussion contrasts Drosophila findings with mammalian findings.

claim: Each neuroblast clone had highly stereotyped projections suggesting that neuroblast identity determines neuroblast-specific projection patterns.
source: Yet the observation that each neuroblast clone had highly stereotyped projections suggests that neuroblast identity (determined by the spatial position of the neuroblast) determines neuroblast-specific projection patterns.
evidence: The discussion interprets the stereotyped projections.

claim: Pioneering work on Drosophila third instar larval neuroblast lineages showed that each neuroblast lineage is composed of two hemilineages with different projection patterns and neurotransmitter expression.
source: Pioneering work on Drosophila third instar larval neuroblast lineages showed that each neuroblast lineage is composed of two hemilineages with different projection patterns and neurotransmitter expression (Harris et al., 2015; Lacin and Truman, 2016; Truman et al., 2010).
evidence: The discussion cites prior work on larval hemilineages.

claim: The NotchON hemilineage always projected to the dorsal/motor neuropil, whereas the NotchOFF hemilineage always projected to the ventral/sensory neuropil.
source: Surprisingly, the NotchON hemilineage always projected to the dorsal/motor neuropil, whereas the NotchOFF hemilineage always projected to the ventral/sensory neuropil.
evidence: The discussion describes the consistent projection pattern.

claim: Neuropil gradients of Slit and Netrin exist along the mediolateral axis.
source: Elegant work has identified neuropil gradients of Slit and Netrin along the mediolateral axis (Zlatic et al., 2009), Semaphorins along the dorsoventral axis (Zlatic et al., 2009), and Wnt5 along the anteroposterior axis (Yoshikawa et al., 2003).
evidence: The discussion cites prior work on guidance cues.

claim: Neurons in a hemilineage projecting to a common region of the neuropil strongly suggests that all neurons within a hemilineage respond in the same way to global pathfinding cues.
source: Our finding that neurons in a hemilineage project to a common region of the neuropil strongly suggests that all neurons within a hemilineage respond in the same way to these global pathfinding cues.
evidence: The discussion interprets the hemilineage projection findings.

claim: Neurons in different hemilineages targeting distinct regions of the neuropil suggests that each hemilineage expresses a different palette of guidance receptors.
source: Conversely, our finding that neurons in different hemilineages target distinct regions of the neuropil suggests that each hemilineage expresses a different palette of guidance receptors, which enable them to respond differentially to the same global cues.
evidence: The discussion interprets the differential targeting findings.

claim: Notch signaling within the Vsx1 + V2 progenitor lineage generates NotchOFF V2a excitatory interneurons and NotchON V2b inhibitory interneurons, which may be distinct hemilineages.
source: Notch signaling within the Vsx1 + V2 progenitor lineage generates NotchOFF V2a excitatory interneurons and NotchON V2b inhibitory interneurons, which may be distinct hemilineages (Del Barrio et al., 2007; Francius et al., 2016; Peng et al., 2007; Skaggs et al., 2011).
evidence: The discussion cites prior work on vertebrate hemilineages.

claim: Both V2a and V2b putative hemilineages contain molecularly distinct subclasses.
source: Interestingly, both V2a and V2b putative hemilineages contain molecularly distinct subclasses (Harris et al., 2019); our work raises the possibility that these subtypes arise from temporal patterning within the V2 lineage.

source: In adults, activation of each larval hemilineage from NB5-2 showed similar behavioral output, whereas each hemilineage from NB6-1 elicited different behaviors (Harris et al., 2015).

source: Interestingly, the three-dimensional location of each hemilineage temporal cohort synaptic cluster is identical on the left and right side of A1 (data not shown), ruling out the mechanism of stochastic self-avoidance (Zipursky and Grueber, 2013).

source: We favor the model that hemilineages direct gross neurite targeting to motor or sensory neuropil, whereas temporal identity acts combinatorially with each hemilineage to direct more precise neurite targeting and synaptic connectivity.

claim: Lineage information, hemilineage identity, and temporal identity can all be accurately predicted using morphological features.
source: We show that lineage information, hemilineage identity, and temporal identity can all be accurately predicted using morphological features (e.g., number of fascicles entering the neuropil for neuroblast clones and radial position for temporal cohorts).
evidence: The discussion summarizes the methodological findings.

claim: Lineage, hemilineage, and temporal identity act sequentially to progressively refine neuronal projections, synapse localization, and connectivity.
source: We find that lineage, hemilineage, and temporal identity act sequentially to progressively refine neuronal projections, synapse localization, and connectivity, and our data supports a model where hemilineage-temporal cohorts are units of connectivity for assembling motor circuits.
evidence: The discussion summarizes the main conclusion.

claim: The study analyzed 160 interneurons, 56 motor neurons, and 86 sensory neurons, which corresponded to approximately 25% of all inputs and 14% of all outputs for the 12 hemilineages.

claim: Connectivity is similar for hemilineages in A1L and A1R.
source: We found similar connectivity for the same neurons on the left and right side of the segment (Figure 7A–C), validating the accuracy of the neuronal reconstructions as well as the stereotypy of neurogenesis.

claim: Neurons in a hemilineage were clustered together in network space, suggesting that hemilineage-related neurons are highly interconnected and functionally distinct.
source: Consistent with anatomical observations, we found that neurons in a hemilineage were clustered together in network space, suggesting that hemilineage-related neurons are highly interconnected and functionally distinct (Figure 7D–F), similar to what has been suggested previously (Harris et al., 2015).
evidence: The results section describes network clustering.

claim: Neurons within a hemilineage had a lower network distance (i.e., greater connectivity) than unrelated neurons.
source: Importantly, neurons within a hemilineage had a lower network distance (i.e., greater connectivity) than unrelated neurons, while neurons within a hemilineage-temporal cohort had a lower network distance than those related by hemilineage alone (Figure 7G–J).
evidence: The results section describes connectivity distances.

claim: Neurons within a hemilineage-temporal cohort had a lower network distance than those related by hemilineage alone.
source: Importantly, neurons within a hemilineage had a lower network distance (i.e., greater connectivity) than unrelated neurons, while neurons within a hemilineage-temporal cohort had a lower network distance than those related by hemilineage alone (Figure 7G–J).
evidence: The results section describes connectivity distances for temporal cohorts.

claim: Less than 20% of hemilineage-related or hemilineage-temporal cohort-related neurons were directly connected.
source: Interestingly, we found that the largest difference between hemilineage and hemilineage-temporal cohort connectivity was at the two synapse distance. While less than 20% of hemilineage-related or hemilineage-temporal cohort-related neurons were directly connected, 75% of hemilineage-temporal cohort neurons were separated by two synapses or less (Figure 7I, J).
evidence: The results section provides quantitative connectivity data.
